newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wants accused Cosby extortionist.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wants accused Cosby extortionist.

text.p: An arrest warrant in a Kansas fraud case has been issued for a man already in prison in New York for allegedly trying to extort $40 million from Bill Cosby, a federal prosecutor said Thursday.
News of the warrant against Jose Medina, 51, of Bethesda, Ohio, came during a bail hearing in the Cosby extortion case pending in Manhattan federal court.

Medina had been convicted in Johnson County, Kansas, in 1990 for loan brokering and theft by deception. When Kansas authorities learned of the charges against Medina in the Cosby case, they issued an arrest warrant for violating his probation terms.
At the end of the bail hearing, U.S. Magistrate Judge Andrew Peck ruled that Medina had not met the conditions of his bail terms and could not yet be released.

Medina had been arrested Jan. 18 with Autumn Jackson, 22, on charges they demanded money from Cosby to refrain from selling a tabloid newspaper a story alleging that Jackson is the entertainer's illegitimate daughter.
On Tuesday Antonay Williams, who describes himself as Jackson's boyfriend, pleaded guilty for his role in the scheme and agreed to cooperate with authorities.

Last week U.S. Magistrate Judge Andrew Peck approved a bail package for Medina and Jackson that allowed for their release on a $250,000 personal recognisance bond co-signed by two financially responsible people.
Jackson was released Monday night after obtaining the necessary signatures.

Medina has remained in prison while his lawyer, Neil Checkman, tried to get two people to guarantee his bond. Last week Medina's employer, Dixie Dunn, an occupational therapist in whose home he has been living since at least 1989, agreed to provide a signature.

Checkman told Peck during the hearing that Dunn's sister has also agreed to guarantee the bond. But Assistant U.S. Attorney Lewis Liman provided evidence that the sister had insufficient assets to cover the amount.
He also told Peck that even if Medina were released, he would immediately be arrested on the Kansas warrant for violating his probation terms.
